clue.text: Altered course in spring

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A river or route changed its path during the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is the place water rises from.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is where a stream rises, its point of origin, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Raised a lot of money with hotel worker for strike

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something turns it upwards, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal of it
a page is a uniformed boy who runs errands in a hotel

explanation.surface: Someone raised a fortune with a hotel employee's help to fund a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like fundraising, but it tells you to turn the money word upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a stoppage of work, a halt organised by workers as a protest.

clue.text: Reduce consumption in vain

parts.note: consumption of something is its use
to reduce is to have less

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut back on what we consume, dismissed as futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce consumption' reads as the phrase USE LESS, which run together becomes one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in vain achieves nothing, and so is futile or pointless.

clue.text: Island crop one delivered in early January

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A harvest from an island shipped out at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests shipping a crop, but here it means born: the star sign runs from late December to mid-January.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby born in early January has the zodiac sign of the goat, so is called by that sign's name.

clue.text: Stress that's central to unease MP has, I submit

indicators.note: central to says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across these words, after the first three of unease and before the end of submit

explanation.surface: A politician's anxiety is causing stress, someone argues.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a word or idea is emphasis, the special importance given to it.

clue.text: Help employee's expecting to get for labour

definitions.text: Help employee's expecting to get for labour

parts.words: Help employee's expecting to get for labour
parts.note: surface reading: the assistance a worker hopes to receive for their work
setter's reading: the employee is expecting a baby, and labour is childbirth, so this is time off granted for having a child

explanation.surface: A worker anticipates some support in return for their toil.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'expecting' and 'labour' have a pregnancy sense hiding behind their work sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid time off given to an employee around the birth of her baby is the benefit described.

clue.text: Create stink over article prone to being erroneous

parts.note: to hum is slang for to smell bad
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Kicking up a fuss about a newspaper piece that is often wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' places the first piece above the second in this down entry. The definition echoes the saying 'to err is human'.
explanation.definitionFit: As the proverb 'to err is human' says, people are fallible, liable to make mistakes.

clue.text: Pungent wit and anger making one cross, sort of

parts.note: salt is sharp, biting wit, as in 'Attic salt'
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Sharp remarks and temper make a person annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, matching the surface, but it is the X-shaped figure, as on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross in heraldry, St Andrew's being the best-known example.

clue.text: Ramshackle dwelling for number of crewmen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crude, rickety hut
second meaning: a sea song sung by sailors as they work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a count of sailors, but it is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tumbledown shack and a sailors' work song, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Part of US law — revised its draft with people twice intervening

indicators.note: intervening means coming in between, so these pieces are placed inside the rearranged letters
a revised text has been reworked, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
men are people
the people word is used a second time

explanation.surface: A part of American law was redrafted with people repeatedly getting involved.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the opening amendment of the US Constitution, guaranteeing free speech, press and religion.

clue.text: Add to what's on page in report, possibly inserting verse

indicators.note: inserting means putting something inside, so the poetry abbreviation goes within
possibly suggests one of many arrangements, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: Putting some poetry into a document to supplement what is already written.
explanation.definitionFit: To overprint is to print extra matter on top of something already printed on a page.

clue.text: Whiskey from Islay and a different island

definitions.note: different because Islay, in the wordplay, is also an island

parts.note: Islay, a Scottish island, is famous for its single malt whisky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dram from one Scottish island alongside another island.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation, an island other than Islay.

clue.text: Negligent on parking — that's what starts argument

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
remiss means careless or negligent

explanation.surface: Careless parking is the thing that sets off a row.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the first piece after the second. 'Argument' is a chain of logic, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss (or premise) is a proposition from which a line of reasoning begins.

clue.text: Wrecked train, or went off the rails

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is smashed apart, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A train crashed, or derailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the rails' fits the train picture, but here it means behaving wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to act without restraint, which is going off the rails in the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Gadget produced by American fighter's second

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, and the 's is kept
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A device made by a US soldier's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a boxer's helper, but it is a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo (or gizmo) is an informal word for a clever device or contraption.

clue.text: Where to locate lots of fliers, by means of putting sign outside

definitions.text: Where to locate lots of fliers

indicators.note: putting one thing outside another means it wraps around the preceding piece

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac
via means by way of or by means of

explanation.surface: Advice on where to station a crowd of leafleteers or pilots by posting a notice outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' suggests leaflets or pilots, but here they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviaries are large enclosures for keeping birds, so they house many creatures that fly.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed about English journalists being put down

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the colour word goes around what follows

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
E is the abbreviation for English
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Blushing because English reporters are being snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Put down in the sense of crushed or held down by force means suppressed, kept in check.

clue.text: Revolutionary can read about left in annual publication

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation
something revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A radical is able to read about the political left in a yearly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is printed afresh every year, listing the days and months of that year.

clue.text: It's perilous guarding monarch and court

indicators.note: guarding something means enclosing it protectively, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: chancy means risky or perilous
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: Danger surrounds the king and his royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a royal court, but it is a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court, historically the Lord Chancellor's court.

clue.text: Natural surroundings, some with a bit attached

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a part of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of with into attached

explanation.surface: A natural setting with something extra tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Support with work backing speakers' positions

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the joined pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: to aid is to support
OP, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Help with a job that endorses people giving speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like more support, but it reverses everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia are raised platforms, the places where speakers and conductors stand.

clue.text: Make preliminary plan for man that might become king

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sketch out, a variant spelling of draft
second meaning: a piece in the board game ... (checkers), crowned king on reaching the far side

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' and 'king' suggest a royal heir, but they are pieces in the board game, which Americans call checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a British spelling of draft, a rough plan, and a single counter in the game of draughts.

clue.text: China is protecting border, first of all

indicators.note: protecting means shielding all round, so the friend word wraps around the edge word

parts.note: china means mate, from rhyming slang china plate
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: China guarding its frontier is the top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or earliest, coming first of all in time.

clue.text: Provided with new cover, make a comeback

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as a book given a fresh binding
second meaning: to recover or spring back

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as RE-BOUND, bound again.
explanation.definitionFit: A book bound again has a new cover, and to spring back after a setback is to recover.

clue.text: Without any qualifications, say

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to speak or pronounce

explanation.walkthrough: 'Without any qualifications' suggests someone lacking diplomas, but it means unreserved.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means total or unconditional; as a verb it means to speak.

clue.text: Make happy about everyone's first 25% raise

indicators.note: about means around, so the happiness word surrounds the kept letters

parts.note: to elate is to make very happy

indicators.note: a quarter at the start means keeping only that opening portion and losing the rest

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters long

explanation.surface: Cheer up by giving all staff a quarter more pay.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter of an eight-letter word is its first two letters. '25% raise' reads as a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Church music assembled, including Biblical section

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the Bible section goes inside

parts.note: people who assembled met
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A choir piece put together with a passage from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, usually sacred and unaccompanied, sung in church.

clue.text: Became green, supposedly, holding fuel back as foreseen

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the green-eyed word wraps the fuel word

parts.note: envy is proverbially green, the green-eyed monster

indicators.note: back says the fuel word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone turned green, perhaps, keeping fuel in reserve as predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Envisaged means imagined as a future possibility, so pictured in advance or foreseen.

clue.text: Learned line to repeat

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Memorised a line for repeating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' reads as a verb but is the adjective meaning educated.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person is educated and well-read, which is the adjective sense of learned.

clue.text: Person working on text partly changed it, originally

indicators.note: partly means only in part, so the letters are a portion of the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of changed into the start of originally

explanation.surface: Someone revising a document altered it a little from the original.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes exactly what such a person does, which makes the hidden word easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor prepares and corrects written material before publication.
